findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison coordinate contrasts at the observed selection nodes and over the complete observed window are strongest for the short-range pair-distance shell densities: pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z 0.631, q 2.2e-5, positive batch fraction 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z 0.540, q 9.8e-5, positive batch fraction 1.0). The same features carry the largest branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations (branch_adjusted:163/164/240/241) and the largest adjusted raw-covariance effects (branch_adjusted:86/87). These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a radial shell-density observable, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not an interaction energy.

The long-range shell pair_kernel_7.0 has the opposite sign to the short-range shells (endpoint_effects:13, integrated z -0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0), with a negative branch-adjusted raw correlation (branch_adjusted:167) and a negative adjusted correlation (branch_adjusted:244). This is a signed contrast on a distinct observable, so it cannot be averaged with the short-range shells into a single quality axis.

Landmark soft-minimum distances and occupancy shells show mixed signs across landmarks: landmark_00_softmin is negative (endpoint_effects:14, z -0.481, positive batch fraction 0.0) while landmark_00_occupancy3 is positive (endpoint_effects:15, z 0.545, positive batch fraction 1.0); landmark_06_softmin is positive (endpoint_effects:32, z 0.294) while landmark_06_occupancy5 is negative (endpoint_effects:34, z -0.365); landmark_18_softmin is positive (endpoint_effects:68, z 0.264) while landmark_18_occupancy5 is negative (endpoint_effects:70, z -0.311). The adjusted-covariance landmark effects (branch_adjusted:145, 222, 299, 301) retain the same sign pattern. Soft-minimum distance and shell occupancy are different observables and their signs cannot be pooled.

Global shape components are signed and mostly negative: shape_xx (endpoint_effects:3, z -0.495, q 8.1e-4), shape_yy (endpoint_effects:4, z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0), shape_zz (endpoint_effects:5, z -0.183) and shape_yz (endpoint_effects:8, z -0.212). The shape_yy contrast is the most reproducible of these (branch_adjusted:158 raw correlation, branch_adjusted:235 adjusted correlation). These are pose/shape descriptors, not local coordinate information.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible negative effects in the branch-adjusted table: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are negative under both raw and adjusted covariance (branch_adjusted:74/76 and 151/153) and under raw and adjusted correlation (branch_adjusted:228/230 and 305/307), with same-sign batch fractions of 0.93-1.0. joint_translation_RMS_A is also negative but weaker (branch_adjusted:75/152/229/306). These are joint pose diagnostics, not local coordinate information.

Within-selector joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment (joint_diagnostics:1, mean 0.092, q 2.2e-9) and with teacher innovation-contrast alignment (joint_diagnostics:11, mean 0.226, q 2.2e-9), but negatively associated with observed child score gain (joint_diagnostics:2, mean -0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is predominantly internal rather than rigid (joint_diagnostics:14, internal fraction 0.787). These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit.

Available descendant survival credit is positive for several landmark soft-mass and occupancy features (survival_effects:0 landmark_00_soft_mass z 0.365; survival_effects:70 landmark_07_soft_mass z 0.220; survival_effects:100 landmark_10_soft_mass z 0.234; survival_effects:186 landmark_18_local_czz z 0.217) and negative for several local covariance components (survival_effects:46 landmark_04_local_czz z 0.266 positive; survival_effects:56 landmark_05_local_czz z -0.419; survival_effects:96 landmark_09_local_czz z -0.390; survival_effects:146 landmark_14_local_czz z -0.308; survival_effects:156 landmark_15_local_czz z -0.399). This is recorded joint-head survival credit, not decoded terminal affinity benefit.

Decoded terminal learning labels are not available (decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false; clocks label_semantics is 'Recorded affinities removed; equal score prior'). The lineage support table records terminal metadata at score time 0.99 and state time 1.0, outside the observed learning window [0.0, 0.5]. Therefore last-record survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-selection versus descendant-credit comparison is unavailable.

Turnover accounting separates population-rate, edge-rate and turnover-residual-rate components. For several features the edge rate and the turnover residual have opposite signs (e.g. landmark_00_local_cxx turnover:13 edge -4.34 vs turnover:14 residual +4.29; landmark_00_local_cyy turnover:16 edge -4.79 vs turnover:17 residual +5.05; landmark_04_local_cxx turnover:133 edge -4.60 vs turnover:134 residual +5.67; landmark_07_local_cxx turnover:223 edge -4.69 vs turnover:224 residual +5.08; landmark_08_local_cxx turnover:253 edge -5.12 vs turnover:254 residual +5.54; landmark_16_local_cyy turnover:496 edge -5.90 vs turnover:497 residual +6.37; landmark_17_local_cxx turnover:523 edge -4.82 vs turnover:524 residual +5.24; landmark_19_local_cxx turnover:583 edge -4.82 vs turnover:584 residual +5.30). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

Observed-node linear trends over the complete observed window are available for landmark_00 features (continuous:0-9) and the full set of landmark and pair-kernel features (continuous:0-199), with first and last rate z values and sign-change counts. The curve-support audit reports relative node RMSE of 0.29-0.93 and strong sign-conflict node counts of 0-15 across the audited features, and no Legendre runtime is allowed. These trends are coordinate contrasts, not trajectory velocity forces.

The information audit reports compressed-choice excess fixed RMS of 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092), compressed-choice fixed RMS of 0.564 A, compressed-choice proper-rigid RMS of 0.529 A, top-4 teacher overlap of 0.470, and compressed-chosen teacher score correlation of 0.102 (CI 0.065-0.140). The teacher modes table lists 28 teachers with assignment RMS quantiles 0.446/0.863/1.050 A and temperature_edits false. These are observational teacher-agreement diagnostics, not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor.

Global centroid components are weak and inconsistent: raw-covariance centroid effects are near zero with p 0.55-0.95 (branch_adjusted:0-2), adjusted-covariance centroid effects are also near zero (branch_adjusted:77-79), and endpoint centroid contrasts are small (endpoint_effects:0-2, integrated z -0.111 to -0.061). No centroid direction is supported as a reproducible coordinate rule.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: the short-range pair-distance shell densities (pair_kernel_1.5, 2.5, 3.5) are the most reproducible signed coordinate contrasts at the observed selection nodes and over the complete observed window, with consistent positive batch fractions and the largest branch-adjusted correlations. Observable: pair_kernel_a for a in {1.5, 2.5, 3.5} A. Intended response: increase in the favorable-minus-comparison contrast. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Spatial scale: pair distances 1.5-3.5 A. Discriminating failure: a batch-level sign reversal or a null adjusted correlation for these shells.

Hypothesis: the long-range shell pair_kernel_7.0 carries a reproducible negative contrast that is distinct from the short-range shells. Observable: pair_kernel_7.0. Intended response: decrease in the favorable-minus-comparison contrast. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Spatial scale: pair distances near 7 A. Discriminating failure: a positive batch fraction above 0.5 or a positive adjusted correlation.

Hypothesis: landmark soft-minimum distance and shell occupancy carry opposite signs at the same landmark, so a single landmark region cannot be assigned one direction without specifying the observable. Observable: landmark_XX_softmin versus landmark_XX_occupancy3/occupancy5. Intended response: sign depends on the chosen observable. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Spatial scale: landmark radius 5 A. Discriminating failure: same-sign softmin and occupancy contrasts at the same landmark across batches.

Hypothesis: joint-motion RMS diagnostics (joint_innovation_RMS_A, joint_internal_RMS_A) are reproducible negative contrasts that are distinct from local coordinate information. Observable: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A. Intended response: decrease in the favorable-minus-comparison contrast. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Spatial scale: whole-pose joint motion. Discriminating failure: a positive adjusted correlation or a same-sign batch fraction below 0.5.

Hypothesis: descendant survival credit is positive for landmark soft-mass and occupancy features and negative for several local covariance components, but this credit is recorded joint-head credit and not decoded terminal affinity benefit. Observable: survival_enrichment_z. Intended response: direction depends on the feature. Target origin: observed selection nodes with descendant credit. Spatial scale: landmark radius 5 A. Discriminating failure: decoded terminal labels becoming available and reversing the sign.

Hypothesis: the turnover residual rate is an accounting diagnostic that separates within-path change from changing cohort composition, and its sign can oppose the edge rate for the same feature. Observable: population_rate, edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate. Intended response: not a causal selection effect. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Spatial scale: whole window. Discriminating failure: a residual that is fully explained by reclassification and parent weighting.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles
Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit
Pair kernels, moments and turnover rates are diagnostic evidence only; the executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term
